description: Comparing Ordinal Quality Scores; published open data from the UCI Wine Quality dataset.
observation_unit: One sample of Portuguese vinho verde, red or white, with its sensory quality score: the median of at least three assessments by wine experts on a 0-10 scale.
source: Published open data: Wine Quality (Cortez et al. 2009), UCI Machine Learning Repository; CC BY 4.0.

citation.dataset: Cortez, P., Cerdeira, A., Almeida, F., Matos, T., & Reis, J. (2009). Wine Quality [Dataset]. UCI Machine Learning Repository. https://doi.org/10.24432/C56S3T
citation.article: Cortez, P., Cerdeira, A., Almeida, F., Matos, T., & Reis, J. (2009). Modeling wine preferences by data mining from physicochemical properties. Decision Support Systems, 47(4), 547-553. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.dss.2009.05.016

retrieved.version: UCI record last updated 2023-11-15; archive SHA-256 3ed56667f4b828242bd732d7d1dd7f2861e54432239d7fa63877014cbb0304d4.

filters: The 1,599 rows of winequality-red.csv are placed above the 4,898 rows of winequality-white.csv, each in file order, including rows that repeat another row exactly; wine numbers the 6,497 rows in that order because the source has no identifier.
colour records which of the two files a row came from.
quality is the publisher's sensory score; the 11 physicochemical columns are left out.

columns.name: wine
columns.description: Wine number: red file first, then white, each in file order

columns.name: colour
columns.description: Wine colour, from the file the row came from

columns.name: quality
columns.description: Sensory quality score: median of at least three expert assessments
